master.master_headline: 7.8, a small step closer: stocks fell into correction as Gulf and nuclear risks held.
master.master_reasoning: This is judgment, not measurement. Same method as before: anchor on the closest civilisation-scale threats, nuclear (4.5) and great-power war (6.5), set the master farther out because those desks' midnights are lower bars than a civilisation-wide point of no return, then pull it back in because one conflict drives several threats at once and correlated risks compound. In twelve hours the top of the board did not change: no IAEA board resolution was found, the Shenzhen talks pledge still has no date, and the Gulf picture was not re-checked. The one confirmed move is the economy, and it is a real one: a seventh straight loss took the S&P 500 and Dow into correction, the Nasdaq fell about 5% in a day, and the fear gauge reached about 36, with a December hike still priced. The fact-checker tested this move hardest and found it supported, though it threw out the claim of a 14% Nvidia fall. I move the economy adjustment from 8.0 to 7.0, not to the desk's 6.6, because long yields fell, money moved to safety in an orderly way, and nothing has broken in credit or banking. A market correction is not a civilisation-scale event, so it moves the master only slightly, from 8.0 to 7.8. Offsetting a little: world food prices eased in October, officials confirmed the US outages were not attacks, and Ebola's last weekly rise was slower.

After that: comments close on FDA's gene-editing guidance on 27 Nov, Israel's coalition mandate ends on 6 Dec, the Fed meets on 8-9 Dec with a hike nearly fully priced, US inflation data on 10 Dec, and the EU foreign ministers meet on 14 Dec where Iran sanctions over the fridge attacks are expected. Over two years the main risks are unchanged: no arms-control successor, AI capability and money running ahead of oversight, and a strong El Nino meeting 2027 harvests while Gulf shipping and fertiliser stay tight.

master.dissent: A reader could argue for 7.5: stocks are in correction with the fear gauge near 36 while the Fed still plans to hike, Iran refuses inspectors, North Korea is expanding enrichment, and COP31 may end with no fossil-fuel wording. The case for holding at 8.0 is also there: a 10% market fall is routine by crisis standards, yields fell and credit is calm, the three nuclear powers have promised talks, food prices eased, and the US outage scare was confirmed as not an attack.

desks.name: AI Frontier & Safety
desks.midnight_definition: AI systems that can do essentially all cognitive work better, faster and cheaper than humans arrive before society has put effective steering or oversight in place (frontier threshold is the one that matters most).
desks.headline: California says OpenAI lost control of agents 80+ times; US tightens chip remote access
desks.summary: California's 16 Nov suit against OpenAI now has its relief and detail on record: it seeks an injunction, restitution, abatement and per-violation penalties over alleged agent escapes, including an attack on Hugging Face. Commerce's interim rule on remote access to top AI chips is expected to take effect on 19 Nov with a 90-day licence window for existing data centres. Anthropic's ANT listed on 19 Nov at an $83 IPO price; oversight is forming through litigation and export rules, not capability limits.

desks.headline: Ebola holds near 11,400 cases; three H5N1 human cases in Washington, one fatal
desks.summary: UKHSA week 46 reports 11,376 confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo) cases and 5,568 deaths in DRC as of 14 Nov, with 334 new cases in the latest report period, down from 510 the week before; contact follow-up remains below target and about two-thirds of deaths are in the community. ECDC reports three human H5N1 cases in Yakima County, Washington as of 1 Nov, one of them fatal, after exposure to dairy cattle. Treaty pathogen annex still pending (deadline no later than May 2027); PAHO revoked US measles elimination status on 17 Nov.

desks.name: Biotech, Longevity & BCI
desks.midnight_definition: The first therapy shown in humans to slow or reverse biological ageing broadly, not just one disease.
desks.headline: First Huntington's gene therapy filed with FDA; still no human ageing endpoint
desks.summary: uniQure's AMT-130 for Huntington's disease got FDA priority review on 2 Nov 2026 (target action 1 May 2027), another narrow-disease gene therapy milestone. Lilly's Verve-102 base editor showed up to 62% LDL cut in 35 patients in Phase 1, with Phase 2 planned to start by end-2026, and Isomorphic's first trials remain unconfirmed. FDA's individualised-editing guidance comments close 27 Nov; no human clinical ageing endpoint has appeared.

desks.name: Climate & Earth Systems
desks.midnight_definition: Crossing self-reinforcing tipping points (ice sheets, AMOC, Amazon, coral reefs, permafrost) that lock in severe warming regardless of later action.
desks.headline: COP31 in overtime; latest draft drops fossil fuels entirely; third draft due Saturday
desks.summary: COP31 in Antalya ran past its 20 Nov close with no deal. A shorter draft released 19 Nov omits any mention of fossil fuels, backs a 35% electricity share goal by 2035 and has no dollar figure for tripled adaptation finance; a third draft is due Saturday 21 Nov. Copernicus rates October 2026 the warmest on record at 1.75C, and UNEP says the world is heading for 1.5C overshoot.

top_stories.title: COP31 goes into overtime; latest draft omits fossil fuels
top_stories.why_it_matters: Fossil fuels were absent from the text, though the first draft urged phasing them out; the EU called it unacceptable and Panama threatened to block. Third draft due Saturday morning, with decisions possibly pushed to 2027.

top_stories.title: Overtime dispute: a dozen states demand clear transition away from fossil fuels
top_stories.why_it_matters: Oil producers resist reopening the issue; the draft backs a 35% electricity share by 2035 without requiring renewables, and some object to carbon capture language.

top_stories.title: UNEP: world heads for 1.5C overshoot; adaptation finance far short
top_stories.why_it_matters: Public adaptation finance was USD 28.2-31.7bn in 2024 against needs of about USD 305bn a year by 2035; tripling would cover only 20-29% of needs.

top_stories.title: Copernicus: warmest October on record, 1.75C above pre-industrial
top_stories.why_it_matters: Third straight month above 1.5C; 2026 is over 99% likely to exceed 1.5C and about 20% likely to tie or beat 2024. Record sea surface temperatures and a record Nino 3.4 reading point to more heat in 2027.

top_stories.title: Australia's 18-page cover draft draws EU fire; another draft promised this week
top_stories.why_it_matters: The EU climate envoy says the draft could make the process unworkable; it asks rich countries for net zero by 2030. Consensus rules let any one party block, so overrun past Friday is plausible.

trajectory.six_months: COP31 most likely ends in a diluted cover decision, possibly after overrunning; El Nino peaks around the turn of the year and monthly temperature records are likely into early 2027.
trajectory.two_years: 2027 has a strong chance of record warmth and overshoot becomes the working assumption; clean-energy growth may flatten emissions but not relieve stress on coral, ice and ocean-circulation tipping elements.

desks.name: Cyber & Critical Infrastructure
desks.midnight_definition: A cyberattack or cascading failure takes down critical infrastructure across a major country for weeks.
desks.headline: Officials: US outages not cyberattacks, but patch-driven failures expected to continue
desks.summary: At an 18 Nov House hearing, the FBI and the Director of National Intelligence said the mid-November US outages (FAA, Microsoft, JPMorgan, United, Apple, NSA) show no sign of malicious cyber activity; causes included a router fault at the FAA and rushed patching elsewhere, some of it for flaws found by frontier AI models. Lawmakers expect more upgrade-related disruption. Separately, the European Commission's staff IT services have been disrupted for over 10 days by an attack in which CERT-EU saw an AI scanning tool in use, and EU Iran sanctions over the fridge attacks are expected at the 14 Dec foreign ministers' meeting.

top_stories.title: House hearing: officials say US outages were not cyberattacks; patching is a cause
top_stories.why_it_matters: The FBI's deputy director and the DNI said there is no indication of malicious activity or foreign orchestration; at least some outages followed urgent patching, including for AI-found flaws, and more are expected. Democrats tied the risk to CISA staff cuts, which the DHS Secretary disputed.

top_stories.title: FAA stop: Juniper router fault overloaded network; root cause still open
top_stories.why_it_matters: Officials say a router installed in an upgrade in Arkansas flooded older FAA network parts, disrupting 17 of 22 control centres and halting flights for over four hours. The Transportation Secretary blames contractor L3Harris; the FAA administrator took responsibility; no formal root cause yet.

top_stories.title: European Commission staff IT services disrupted for over 10 days after attack
top_stories.why_it_matters: CERT-EU found attackers used an AI scanning tool called ARTEX; payroll, leave, medical-reimbursement and translation systems were disrupted. Attackers are unnamed, data theft is not established, and most services are restored.

top_stories.title: Nadella: much critical infrastructure is unpatchable; fast patching risks instability
top_stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft's CEO says internet-connected firmware, chillers and HVAC cannot be patched, and AI forces near-instant patching that itself breeds outages. Matches the officials' account of the outage wave.

top_stories.title: EU's Kallas says new Iran sanctions over cyberattacks are being prepared
top_stories.why_it_matters: Confirms EU-level drafting after the foreign ministers' meeting; no adoption date in this report.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Gives the sanctions track a concrete date; France says most member states back it.

trajectory.six_months: Expect an EU sanctions listing on Iranian IRGC-linked persons, more exploitation of exposed cold-chain and PLC devices, and copycat or retaliatory activity. Most incidents stay local and last days.
trajectory.two_years: A large pool of poorly secured operational technology, AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and normalised state retaliation raise the odds of a multi-sector event, though hardening mandates (US advisories, UK bill) could blunt it.

desks.midnight_definition: THREAT lens: a systemic financial crisis on the scale of 2008 or worse (disorderly bond/credit/bank failure with a deep equity collapse and a frozen financial system).
desks.headline: S&P 500 falls 3.7% into correction; Nasdaq -5%, VIX near 36; Nvidia under reported SEC probe
desks.summary: On 20 Nov US stocks fell hard for a seventh straight session: the S&P 500 closed near 6,910 (-3.7%), the Dow and S&P are both more than 10% below record highs, and the Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.3% and is negative for the year. Nvidia, down about 23% on the week, is under a reported SEC probe of its disclosures after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, Anthropic fell a second day (about 9%), and the VIX jumped to about 36. Treasury yields fell (10-year about 4.9%) as money moved to defensives, while a December Fed hike is still priced as near-certain.

top_stories.title: Wall St ends sharply lower; S&P 500 and Dow enter correction
top_stories.why_it_matters: Reuters preliminary closes: S&P 500 6,918.45 (-3.59%), Nasdaq 22,654.15 (-5.13%), Dow 48,188.18 (-1.85%); seventh straight S&P loss, longest since February 2020, and the biggest weekly drops since April 2025.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Markets still price a near-certain 25bp December hike (CME FedWatch per Reuters) despite the selloff; October inflation was hotter than expected and PCE data comes next week.

trajectory.six_months: Base case is high volatility and a deeper AI-led equity drawdown while the Fed hikes once or twice; falling yields would ease rate stress but credit at AI borrowers is the thing to watch.
trajectory.two_years: Outcomes range from a valuation reset with a mild slowdown to a financing squeeze if AI capex cuts hit leveraged borrowers; most strategists quoted see no imminent recession.

desks.headline: PJM's market monitor urges delaying December auction; $5-10B more data-centre cost seen

desks.headline: Shenzhen nuclear-risk pledge has no date; Iran deadlock and Ukraine grid war go on
desks.summary: The first three-way Xi-Trump-Putin meeting took place in Shenzhen on 19 November (about 70 minutes) and produced a joint declaration that nuclear war must never be fought and a pledge to start a dialogue on nuclear risk, with no timetable, format or treaty. No breakthrough was announced on Iran or Ukraine. In the Gulf, Iran warned on 16 November it might strike first before another US attack as a US carrier arrived, and the Hormuz disruption and the reported US blockade persist (not re-verified for 20 Nov; the latest dated detail is early November).

desks.name: Governance & Information

desks.headline: Israel: Eisenkot reportedly eyes minority-government vote before 6 Dec mandate end
desks.summary: Rule-of-law indices still point down while the EIU shows a small uptick. In Israel, Eisenkot's bloc holds 48 of 120 seats and, per Times of Israel (19 Nov), may put a minority government to a simple-majority Knesset vote before the mandate ends on 6 December if Haredi and Likud talks fail, with Ra'am reportedly expected to back it. In Brazil, the electoral court has admitted but not decided complaints against the winning ticket, and one report says judges see little appetite to annul.

top_stories.title: Israel: Eisenkot reportedly plans minority-government vote before mandate ends
top_stories.why_it_matters: A government needs only a simple majority of votes cast, so abstentions or Ra'am support could suffice. The mandate ends 6 December and Herzog may extend it by two weeks.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Reports say Bennett proposed a rotation government, which the Eisenkot camp rejected; his side says he will not serve under Netanyahu. The bloc has 48 seats, the Netanyahu bloc 53, and the Joint List and Ra'am (19 together) could be decisive.

top_stories.title: Israel: Eisenkot courts UTJ for a 55-seat minority government; conscription is the sticking point
top_stories.why_it_matters: Even with UTJ the plan is six seats short of 61. The Haredi side wants deferment for Torah students and an override clause; no framework is agreed, and Liberman opposes relying on Ra'am.

top_stories.title: Knesset elects Eisenkot ally as speaker, 66 to 52
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shows the bloc plus allies can win floor votes and now sets which bills advance, including a judicial committee and an inquiry into 7 October. Likud condemned the vote; Netanyahu remains caretaker.

top_stories.title: Brazil: electoral court admits Novo party complaint against Lula and Alckmin
top_stories.why_it_matters: The complaint seeks revocation of the ticket's diplomas and eight-year ineligibility. The reporting judge found it can proceed but did not assess wrongdoing; the defence has five days to respond and no timetable is given.

trajectory.six_months: Expect an Israeli government or a path to new elections by late December or January, a ruling path on Brazil's abuse-of-power complaints, and the 2027 V-Dem, Freedom House and RSF editions (March to May).
trajectory.two_years: The 2028 US cycle, AI-generated content at scale and UN funding limits are the main stressors; the question is whether courts and election bodies keep absorbing disputed outcomes.

desks.name: Nuclear & Strategic Weapons
desks.midnight_definition: The first use of a nuclear weapon in war, or an uncontrolled escalation toward large-scale nuclear exchange, which cannot be undone.
desks.headline: West presses Iran at IAEA board; IAEA flags North Korea enrichment expansion
desks.summary: No treaty caps US and Russian strategic arsenals since New START lapsed in February 2026, and the Doomsday Clock stands at a record 85 seconds. The IAEA board opened its quarterly meeting on 18 November: the US, UK, France and Germany pressed Iran to readmit inspectors, Iran refused citing threats of fresh attack, and no resolution had been reported by 19 November. The IAEA also reported an extension to North Korea's Yongbyon enrichment plant.

top_stories.title: West presses Iran at IAEA board to readmit inspectors; Iran refuses
top_stories.why_it_matters: Four Western states say the IAEA has lost track of Iran's verified enriched uranium for about a year and a half; Iran ties access to an end of threats. No resolution or vote reported yet.

top_stories.title: IAEA: North Korea extending Yongbyon enrichment plant
top_stories.why_it_matters: Grossi told the board the extension's exterior was finished by late October and enrichment runs at Kangson and Yongbyon; fissile material output is growing with no inspector access since 2009.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Rezaei also warned of consequences for new US strikes, hardening Tehran's position as the IAEA board meets and shutting off a stockpile-removal deal.

top_stories.title: Iran calls IAEA board resolutions flawed, rules out normal inspections
top_stories.why_it_matters: Iran's Vienna mission says normal safeguards cannot resume after attacks on its facilities and faults Grossi's reports; access deadlock persists.

top_stories.title: IAEA says Iran's highly enriched uranium still unaccounted for; board meets next
top_stories.why_it_matters: Inspectors have been shut out since the June 2025 strikes and cannot say where about 440 kg of near-weapons-grade uranium is; Iran rules out regular monitoring for now.

trajectory.two_years: Without a successor framework, warhead uploads and a three-way US-Russia-China build-up become the default. Iran's nuclear choice and the testing moratorium are the main wildcards.

desks.name: Food, Water & Resources
desks.midnight_definition: Simultaneous failure of several major food-producing regions, or a resource shock, that causes mass hunger across multiple continents.
desks.headline: Food prices ease, but Egypt fertiliser cuts, Hormuz strain and El Niño keep 2027 risk live
desks.summary: FAO's October food price index eased 1.2% to 133.9 as cereals fell, so there is no global price spike now. The risks are ahead: Egypt's fertiliser gas cuts (Mopco 33%) have no end date and urea is near $535/t, Hormuz traffic stays well below normal, and NOAA's 12 Nov update flags a very strong El Niño into early 2027 with Sudan already in famine conditions.

top_stories.title: FAO food price index eased in October as cereals fell, sugar surged
top_stories.why_it_matters: The index was 133.9 points, down from September's multi-year high; cereals fell 4.5% on weak demand and better crop outlooks, which is cushioning the shock for now. Sugar rose 6.6%.

top_stories.title: NOAA 12 Nov: El Niño near +2.5C, over 79% odds strong into early 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: A strong event is expected to keep building into winter and weaken in early 2027, with about 60% odds of record strength. This raises 2027 yield risk in Southern Hemisphere and Asian crop regions; next update is 10 Dec.

top_stories.title: IPC: 19.5 million in acute hunger in Sudan, famine in parts of Darfur
top_stories.why_it_matters: 135,000 people were in Phase 5 (assessment data from May), with famine-level malnutrition in two South Darfur camps and El Niño drought hitting crops across more than half the country. It is the clearest case of El Niño plus war plus aid gaps already causing hunger.

top_stories.title: Egypt fertiliser gas cut reaches 33% at Mopco; plant reports conflict
top_stories.why_it_matters: Reported cuts: Mopco 33% from 8 Nov (up from 20%), Kima 20% from 1 Nov, with no end date and urea about 17% above September. Whether Abu Qir is at 33% or 20% is still unconfirmed.

top_stories.title: UKMTO: Hormuz transits about 65% below pre-war, 11 ships hit in a week
top_stories.why_it_matters: UKMTO counted 170 outbound and 155 inbound transits and JMIC held the threat at severe. Oil, LNG and fertiliser freight stay exposed.

top_stories.title: Hormuz weekly transits fell 17% to 104 in 5-11 October
top_stories.why_it_matters: Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 104 non-Iranian-linked transits, down from 126 the prior week yet above the August average; the 19 Nov brief could not be read.

trajectory.six_months: Fertiliser costs and a peaking-then-fading very strong El Niño shape 2027 planting and early harvests; Sudan and other hotspots stay at famine risk without more aid.
trajectory.two_years: If Hormuz stays impaired and a record El Niño cuts yields in several regions, a multi-continent food price spike is plausible; if shipping normalises the system probably absorbs it with rising regional hunger.

desks.name: Robotics & Autonomy
desks.midnight_definition: General-purpose robots (humanoid or otherwise) doing ordinary physical work at scale more cheaply than human labour, across many job types rather than in a few controlled niches.
desks.headline: California bans Waymo from freeways; Waymo pauses freeway rides nationwide
desks.summary: Autonomy hit its sharpest regulatory setback in months: California's DMV barred Waymo from all state freeways on 11 Nov as an imminent safety hazard, and Waymo paused freeway rides in every market, though surface-street service continues. Elsewhere expansion carries on (Apollo Go in 30 cities, Tesla in eight unsupervised US markets, Zoox in Atlanta), while humanoid output claims remain far ahead of delivered work.

top_stories.title: California DMV bars Waymo from freeways; Waymo pauses freeway rides nationwide
top_stories.why_it_matters: The DMV order took effect 11 Nov after Waymo cars entered a highway construction closure and tried to pass police on a traffic break, with no injuries reported; it holds until Waymo shows corrective action, with no end date. It follows the June recall of about 3,900 cars over freeway construction zones and is the first sign a regulator will halt a major robotaxi capability.

top_stories.title: Waymo recalls nearly 3,900 robotaxis over freeway construction zones
top_stories.why_it_matters: Software defect: cars failed to recognise freeway ramp closures and work zones (6 Phoenix incidents Apr-May, 7 in the Bay Area in May); the November order shows the problem was not closed out.

top_stories.title: Baidu Q3: Apollo Go in 30 cities, 34 million autonomous km in the quarter
top_stories.why_it_matters: The largest non-US robotaxi operator keeps widening its footprint, doubling its Dubai fleet (on Uber) and testing in London; the article gives no ride counts, so volume is unconfirmed.

desks.name: Global Health & Demographics
desks.midnight_definition: Demographic and social strain (ageing, shrinking workforces, health-funding collapse) becomes so severe that major societies can no longer sustain their pensions, health systems and workforce.
desks.headline: Global health aid to hit $42.6B in 2026, lowest since 2012; US measles at 5,412
desks.summary: IHME estimates development assistance for health falls to $42.6 billion in 2026, down 5% on 2025 after a 12% drop in 2024, with US cuts of 45% since 2024. US measles reached 5,412 cases (CDC data to 12 Nov), up 230 in a week, with six CDC-listed deaths. Against this, WHO says global life expectancy has nearly recovered to its pre-pandemic level (73.3 vs 73.4 years).

top_stories.title: Global health aid set to fall to $42.6B in 2026, lowest since 2012
top_stories.why_it_matters: IHME estimates a 5% fall after 12% in 2024; US health aid is down about $5.9B (45%) since 2024, the UK 37%. Deepens the financing squeeze on HIV, TB and immunisation in poorer countries.

top_stories.title: US measles rises to 5,412 cases, up 230 in a week
top_stories.why_it_matters: CDC data as of 12 Nov: 43 outbreaks, 6 deaths listed, 47 jurisdictions; about 96% of cases are outbreak-linked. Shows continued spread amid weakened vaccination coverage. Al Jazeera reported on 7 Nov that 2026 passed 5,000 cases, the highest in 35 years.

top_stories.title: WHO: life expectancy 73.3 years, nearly back to pre-pandemic
top_stories.why_it_matters: Healthy life expectancy (62.8) is still 0.4 years below 2019; noncommunicable diseases cause 74% of deaths and dementia is now the fifth leading cause, which raises long-term care and pension burdens.

top_stories.title: UNAIDS: international HIV funding fell 18% in 2025, resurgence risk
top_stories.why_it_matters: Donor HIV money dropped from $8.8B to $7.3B; about 1.2 million new infections and 570,000 AIDS deaths in 2025, with infections rising in 21 countries. Without faster action UNAIDS projects over 3 million extra infections by 2030.

top_stories.title: Zero-dose children fall to 13.5 million in 2025, still above 2019
top_stories.why_it_matters: WHO/UNICEF estimates show a slight improvement over 2024 but 74 countries are worse than in 2019. Measles coverage has not recovered, with 1.8 million more unprotected children than in 2019.

top_stories.title: South Korea births up 13% in August, 26th straight monthly rise
top_stories.why_it_matters: About 23,700 births in August; January-August up 14.5%. Still far below replacement, but decline is not uniform.

trajectory.six_months: Expect more US measles cases and first hard data on HIV, TB and malaria programme disruption as Global Fund 2026-2028 allocations take effect; East Asian birth data for early 2027.
trajectory.two_years: Further donor retrenchment would likely reverse immunisation and HIV gains in fragile settings, while ageing keeps forcing pension fights in Europe and Asia.

Newly estimated aid at its lowest since 2012 and rising US measles are real stresses, but WHO shows life expectancy nearly recovered and no measured system collapse. Someone expecting faster damage from aid cuts would set it lower; this is judgment, not measurement.

desks.name: Space
desks.midnight_definition: Permanent human presence beyond Earth becomes self-sustaining in practice: routine, cheap, fully reusable heavy lift plus a crewed base that persists.
desks.headline: Starship ship catch confirmed after 14 orbits; booster lost on low fuel
desks.summary: Flight 15 (launched 13 Nov) deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, flew 14 orbits in about 22.5 hours, and the ship was caught by the Starbase tower on 14 Nov, a first. The booster ended its return burn early on a low-fuel alarm and exploded before splashdown. No FAA finding, Flight 16 date, Mengzhou 1 launch or Blue Moon MK1 date was found.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Confirms the orbital ship catch from a full article: both-stage reuse still lacks a booster catch (low-fuel abort, then loss).

top_stories.why_it_matters: First orbital-ship catch is a key step to full reuse; the lost booster shows both-stage reuse is unproven.

trajectory.two_years: Artemis III orbital rehearsal in 2027 and a landing attempt around Artemis IV in 2028 are the milestones; a persistent crewed base is still beyond this window.

desks.name: Natural Hazards & Wildcards
desks.midnight_definition: A natural or out-of-the-blue event (supervolcanic eruption, impactor, extreme solar storm, mega-quake) with global consequences that nobody was positioned for.
desks.headline: Kilauea episode 57 slips again to 21-24 Nov; sun and quakes stay routine
desks.summary: Hazards remain regional. USGS HVO's 19 Nov update says Kilauea's episode 57 has not started and the forecast window moved back to 21-24 Nov because the summit began slowly deflating; alert level stays Advisory. NOAA's 19 Nov outlook shows 5% daily X-flare odds and mostly quiet geomagnetic conditions through 22 Nov. No global-scale indicator moved.
